before.title: Convertible top water leaks into trunk and around rear window
before.description: The folding soft top is finicky and a frequent source of leaks. Water enters the trunk through the holes in the rear deck that accept the top's buttress pins (the seals don't fully seal) and through a slit in the trunk-lid hose that hides the top's flip cable. Owners also report wind noise and water at the back window when the top's drive-link socket falls out of adjustment, making the top hard to raise or stow.
before.solution: Reseal or replace the buttress-pin grommets and the trunk-lid cable hose, and clear/route the top's drainage. If the top won't stow or seal, readjust or reconnect the drive-link socket on the convertible top arm. Keep the trunk weatherstrip and rear deck seals in good condition.
symptoms: Water pooling in the trunk after rain or a wash
Water leak/wind noise at the rear window
Top difficult to raise or won't stow fully
Damp carpet behind the seats

before.title: High-pressure fuel pump failure on the GXP (direct-injected 2.0T)
before.description: The direct-injected 2.0L LNF in the Solstice GXP uses a camshaft-driven high-pressure fuel pump that can fail, sometimes with little warning. When the pump loses pressure the engine drops into reduced engine power/limp mode, may misfire, run rough, or stall, and is hard to restart. It is a recognized weak point owners watch for on GXP purchases.
before.solution: Diagnose fuel-rail pressure and replace the high-pressure fuel pump; the pump follower/cam lobe should also be inspected. Owners report total cost is typically several hundred to about $1,200 including labor.
symptoms: Reduced engine power / limp mode
Rough running or misfire
Hard starting or stalling
Loss of boost/power

before.title: Ignition switch can move out of "run," stalling the engine
before.description: The low-detent-torque ignition switch can be jostled out of the run position by a heavy key ring, knee contact, or a rough road, shutting off the engine while driving. When the switch drops to accessory/off, the car loses power steering and power brake assist and the airbags are disabled, which is dangerous at speed. The Solstice was swept into GM's massive ignition-switch recall.
before.solution: Covered under NHTSA recall 14V-355 (GM expanded the recall in 2014 to include 2006-2010 Solstice). Dealers replace the ignition switch free of charge. Until repaired, GM advised drivers to carry only the ignition key with nothing else on the ring.
symptoms: Engine shuts off while driving
Loss of power steering and power brakes when it stalls
Key turns to accessory unexpectedly
Warning lights flicker before stall

proposal.title: Ignition switch can move out of "run," stalling the engine
proposal.description: NHTSA campaign 14V047—not 14V355—supports the frozen ignition-switch safety identity. It covers 2006-2007 Solstice vehicles whose switch can move out of run under key-ring weight or jarring and an expansion for certain 2008-2010 Solstice vehicles that may contain defective service-replacement switches. Moving out of run can shut off the engine and disable airbag deployment. Campaign 14V171 is a separate ignition-lock-cylinder/key-removal rollaway identity and is not substituted for this page.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN and completion history for NHTSA 14V047 with NHTSA and a GM dealer. Until applicability and completion are confirmed, minimize key-ring weight and stop using a switch that moves unexpectedly; if the engine shuts off, steer and brake deliberately to a safe stop. Ask the dealer to confirm the currently available remedy and any charge rather than relying on the 2014 owner letter. Do not buy an ignition switch, cylinder or key set from this page; campaign applicability, prior repair, part number, programming and VIN fitment must be verified first.

before.title: No interior trunk release - trunk becomes impossible to open with a dead battery
before.description: The Solstice has no conventional mechanical/interior trunk (rear deck) release; it opens only electrically via the key fob or door-mounted button. If the battery dies, owners commonly find the trunk locked shut with jumper cables or the battery itself trapped inside. The fob buttons are also known to wear out, compounding the lockout.
before.solution: Restore power by connecting jumper cables or a charger to the underhood remote terminals to operate the release, or use the emergency procedure: remove the left rear wheel and wheelhouse liner, remove the pressure-relief valve, reach in and pull the child-safety release cable to unlatch the deck. Worn fob membranes can be replaced cheaply.
symptoms: Trunk will not open when battery is dead
Key fob trunk button unresponsive
Battery/jumper cables locked inside trunk

before.title: Passenger airbag suppression (PPS) sensor mat fails, disabling passenger airbag
before.description: The Solstice passenger seat uses a flexible PPS sensor mat that decides whether to suppress the front passenger airbag (e.g., for a child). Repeated occupant weight in the same spot bends and cracks the printed conductor in the mat, which can create an open circuit. With an open circuit the system will not deploy the front passenger airbag even for an adult, and the "Service Airbag" light illuminates.
before.solution: Covered under NHTSA recall 17V-061. Dealers inspect the PPS mat; if functioning they add a reinforcement strip, and if not they install a new mat with the reinforcement strip. Owners report the fix has sometimes failed again after a few thousand miles, so verify the airbag status light afterward.
symptoms: Service Airbag warning light on
Passenger airbag-off indicator stays on with an adult seated
Airbag system fault stored

before.title: Rear differential/driveline clunk and gear whine
before.description: Early Solstices are widely reported to develop a driveline clunk on take-up and shifting at low speed, plus a gear whine from the rear differential that changes with throttle. The clunk is partly an inherent design characteristic, but axle clunk/chatter on turns is caused by stick-slip of the limited-slip clutch plates from insufficient friction-modifier additive. GM addressed it with a redesign adding a rigid member to align the differential and driveshaft.
before.solution: GM issued TSBs covering the noise; the common fix for chatter-on-turns is a differential fluid drain and refill with the correct limited-slip additive (owners frequently use Royal Purple or a synthetic with friction modifier). Later cars received the driveline alignment redesign.
symptoms: Clunk when taking off or shifting at low speed
Whine/gear noise from rear that varies with throttle
Chatter or shudder during tight low-speed turns

before.title: "Reduced Engine Power" limp mode from throttle body coking / TAC faults
before.description: As the car ages, carbon "coking" builds up in the electronic throttle body, slowing the throttle plate response. The throttle actuator control (TAC) system detects a correlation fault between pedal and throttle and drops the car into Reduced Engine Power limp mode. A weak battery, corroded engine ground strap, or dirty MAF can trigger the same symptom and false codes.
before.solution: Clean (or replace) the throttle body, clean the MAF, and service the notorious driver-side engine ground strap and battery. A battery disconnect/relearn often clears the fault after cleaning. Persistent faults may require throttle body or pedal-position sensor replacement.
symptoms: "Reduced Engine Power" or "Engine Power Reduced" message
Limp mode / severely limited acceleration
Service traction control light
Rough or hesitant throttle response

before.title: Timing chain and balance shaft chain stretch on the GXP 2.0T (LNF)
before.description: The turbocharged 2.0L Ecotec LNF (Solstice GXP) is prone to timing chain and balance-shaft chain stretch as the plastic guides and tensioner wear. A worn tensioner produces a cold-start rattle; if the chain skips timing on this interference engine it can bend valves or damage pistons. P0016/P0017 (crank/cam correlation) codes typically accompany a stretched chain.
before.solution: Replace the complete timing chain kit along with the balance-shaft chain kit, guides, tensioner, and water pump together since the labor overlaps. Addressing chain noise promptly prevents catastrophic interference-engine damage.
symptoms: Cold-start rattle/clatter from the front of the engine
Check engine light
Rough idle
Loss of power or no-start if timing jumps

before.title: Solstice Trunk Leak with Top Down (Kappa Platform)
before.description: 2006-2009 Solstice (and Saturn Sky/Opel GT — all Kappa platform) has the trunk lid integrate with the soft top stowage; with the top down, the trunk seal is exposed and frequently leaks in rain. Tiny trunk space (only 3.8 cu ft with top stowed) compounds the issue. Water pools at the spare tire area and rusts the floor panel.
before.solution: Inspect trunk seal annually; replace if cracked ($60-$120 part). 3M weatherstrip adhesive helps reseal. Always check spare tire well after heavy rain. Some owners install a small bilge-pump style drain. Permanent fix is to confirm rain gutters at the top stowage area aren't clogged.
symptoms: wet trunk after rain
standing water in spare tire well
mildew smell from trunk

proposal.title: Solstice Trunk Leak with Top Down (Kappa Platform)
proposal.description: This frozen page overlaps pontiac-solstice-convertible-top-water-leaks-into-trunk-around-rear-window but asserts a different unsupported top-down mechanism. Exact record 10025963 supports a 2006-2009 header/A-pillar convertible-top seam leak, not an exposed trunk seal with the top stowed, spare-tire-well pooling, floor rust, a 3.8-cubic-foot causal relationship, clogged rain gutters or a Kappa-wide defect. No exact source supports a bilge-pump drain or universal seal replacement.
proposal.solution: Do not assume that water in the trunk enters through the top-stowage seal. Dry the area and use a controlled sectional water test to trace the entry point across deck seals, lamp/body seams, top interfaces, drains and prior body repair. This page cannot choose the canonical URL or redirect for the overlapping leak identities. Do not buy weatherstrip, adhesive, drains or pumps from this page; entry point, top position, repair procedure, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: overlapping leak identity recognized
trunk entry point reproduced by sections
top-up and top-stowed states compared
canonical URL decision deferred to redirect policy
